custom_steps:
1. Drag the card for {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  2. Click "Undo" on the message.
  3. Read the order of the cards in {Technician-A}'s column.
  4. Refresh the page and read {Technician-A}'s column again.
  5. Click "Tech View" in the display switcher. On {Work-order-4}'s row in the "Unassigned" group, open the "More actions" (…) menu, click "Assign lead technician", then click {Technician-A} in the list.
  6. Click "Undo" on the message.
  7. Refresh the page and look at the "Unassigned" group and {Technician-A}'s group.
  8. Click {Work-order-2} to open the work order, click ⋮ at the top right (next to "New Line"), then "Audit Log", and read the two newest "Lead tech changed" entries in the Work Order Log.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-2} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-2} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 2: the message closes, {Work-order-2} goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button. No question about scheduled shifts appears.
  • Step 3: the cards read {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}, from the top, as before.
  • Step 4: after the refresh the column still reads {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}, from the top.
  • Step 5: the dialog closes, {Work-order-4} moves into {Technician-A}'s group and the message "{Work-order-4} assigned to {Technician-A}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 6: the message closes, {Work-order-4} goes back to the "Unassigned" group and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button.
  • Step 7: after the refresh {Work-order-4} is still in the "Unassigned" group and not in {Technician-A}'s group.
  • Step 8: the newest entry is the Undo, {Technician-B} → {Technician-A}, and the one before it is {Technician-A} → {Technician-B}. Both show your user and the time.

Slavcho Mitrov (developer), 28 Oct 2026, on how he automates this test: “a Board View drag, then Undo; and the Tech View “Assign lead technician” dialog, then Undo. Each is checked again after a reload. The Audit Log part is covered by a backend test.” The steps follow his; step 8 keeps the Audit Log check for the manual tester.

Known problem (SV-11567, in Code Review on 28 Oct 2026, fast follow; Undo is its own ticket, Chris Ward on SV-11524, 20 Oct 2026; seen on the QA branch sv11524 on 26 Oct 2026): the message has the right words but no "Undo" button, only a close (×), and it closes after about 2.6 seconds. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, Undo has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.
